questions.q: What is the five-part structure this lesson recommends for walking someone through this capstone?
options: Business problem, architecture, design decisions, the finished result, what you'd improve next
Resume, cover letter, references, salary expectations, start date
SQL Server, SSIS, warehouse, SSRS, Power BI — with no mention of decisions or results
Introduction, small talk, technical questions, behavioral questions, closing
questions.explain: Every strong project walkthrough covers the problem, the architecture, the decisions behind it, what it actually produces, and an honest next iteration — in that order.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why is the 'what would you improve next' part of the walkthrough not optional?
options: Interviewers ask it regardless, and having a specific answer ready is the difference between sounding reflective and sounding caught off guard
It's required by the SSRS report's design
It's the only part interviewers actually care about
It replaces the need to explain the architecture at all
questions.explain: Interviewers ask 'what would you do differently' whether you volunteer it or not — a real, specific answer prepared in advance beats improvising one under pressure.

questions.q: What is the recommended way to talk about leaving Production.Location out of the model?
options: As a deliberate scope decision — it lives at a finer grain than the fact table, and including it would have forced the grain to break or an arbitrary rule to be picked
By avoiding the topic entirely in case it comes up
By apologizing for not having time to finish the model
By claiming Production.Location doesn't exist in AdventureWorks2012
questions.explain: Framing it as reasoning about grain, rather than an apology for an unfinished gap, shows the same judgment an interviewer wants to see applied to their own team's real data.

questions.q: Which four things does this lesson recommend actually screen-sharing during a live walkthrough, rather than just describing?
options: The architecture diagram, one control flow view of WorkOrderETL.dtsx, the rendered SSRS report, and the Power BI dashboard's trend and on-time visuals
Every SSIS package's full control flow, line by line
The full DDL for every staging and dimension table
The deployment scripts for SSIS, SSRS, and Power BI in full
questions.explain: Screen time is scarce — the lesson recommends showing the few artifacts that prove the project works, and describing the rest in a sentence instead of demonstrating it live.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a design decision should be explained with a reason, not just named?
options: Because naming a term without explaining why it was needed sounds memorized, while a reason sounds understood
Because interviewers never ask about design decisions
Because naming terms is against best practice in a portfolio review
Because reasons take longer to say than names, which fills more interview time
questions.explain: Saying 'accumulating snapshot fact' without explaining why the design needed one reads as a memorized term. Explaining the reason shows real understanding of the decision.
